list.description: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC applications that delegate authentication to Qeet ID. Confidential apps receive a client secret on registration; public apps use PKCE.
list.searchPlaceholder: Search applications by name, client ID or scope…
list.emptyDescription: Register an OAuth / OIDC application to get started. Define your application, set redirect URIs, and configure the required scopes.
list.emptyDescriptionFiltered: Try a different search term, or clear the filters to see every registered application.

help.docsDescription: Learn how to integrate with Qeet ID

credentials.title: Client credentials for {{name}}
credentials.description: Copy the secret now — it’s bcrypt-hashed server-side after this and can’t be shown again.

delete.title: Delete this application?
delete.descriptionBulk_one: {{count}} application will be deleted. Every app using its client ID will immediately stop being able to authenticate. This can’t be undone.
delete.descriptionBulk_other: {{count}} applications will be deleted. Every app using their client IDs will immediately stop being able to authenticate. This can’t be undone.
delete.confirmDescription: Apps using the client ID for {{name}} will immediately stop being able to authenticate. This can’t be undone.

create.title: Register OAuth / OIDC application
create.description: Create an OIDC client. Confidential clients receive a one-time client secret.
create.name: Name
create.nameHelp: A friendly name to identify this application in your organization.
create.typePublicHelp: Public clients run in browsers or mobile apps and use PKCE. They do not receive a client secret.
create.typeConfidentialHelp: Confidential clients run on a server that can keep a secret. They receive a client secret on registration.
create.publicCalloutBody: PKCE helps protect authorization codes in public clients such as SPAs and mobile apps.
create.confidentialCalloutTitle: The client secret is shown once
create.confidentialCalloutBody: Copy it as soon as it appears — it’s hashed server-side and can’t be shown again. You can rotate it later.
create.redirectUrisHelp: One URL per line. Must be HTTPS in production; localhost is allowed for development.
create.postLogoutUrisHelp: Optional. One URL per line. Users will be redirected here after signing out.
create.scopesHelp: Space-separated list of OAuth scopes. Common scopes include openid, profile, and email.

validation.name: Enter a name.
validation.redirectUris: Add at least one redirect URI.
validation.uri: Enter one full URL per line.

detail.notFoundDescription: It may have been deleted, or you may not have permission to view it. Use the back link above to return to the list.
detail.name: Name
detail.secretDescription: Rotating invalidates the current secret immediately. The new value is shown once.
detail.secretCopyHint: Copy it now — it’s bcrypt-hashed server-side and can’t be shown again.
detail.dangerZoneDescription: Deleting stops every app using this client ID from authenticating.

proofKey.title: Proof key (PKCE)
proofKey.required: Every sign-in must send a proof key (PKCE, S256) and, when it asks for openid, a nonce. Requests without them are refused.
proofKey.exemptUntil: Exempt until {{date}}: sign-ins may leave out the proof key and nonce until then. After that, they must send them.
proofKey.ended: Its exemption ended on {{date}}. Every sign-in must now send a proof key (PKCE, S256) and, with openid, a nonce.

secretFailures.title: Secret attempts
secretFailures.description: Wrong client secrets presented for this application, newest first. Too many in a short time lock it out for a while; the right secret then fails too, with the same answer.
secretFailures.lockedUntil: Locked out until {{date}}: every request authenticating as this application is refused until then.

detail.deleteConfirmDescription: Apps using the client ID for {{name}} will immediately stop being able to authenticate. This can’t be undone.

rotateConfirm.title: Rotate client secret?
rotateConfirm.description: A new client secret is generated immediately and the current one stops working. Update the client application with the new secret.
rotateConfirm.label: Rotate secret

quickstart.title: Integrate this application
quickstart.description: Drop the snippet into your app to add “Sign in with Qeet ID”, then test the flow.
quickstart.testLoginHelp: “Test login” opens the hosted sign-in for this app and returns to its first redirect URI ({{uri}}).
quickstart.testLoginHelpNone: “Test login” opens the hosted sign-in for this app and returns to its first redirect URI (none set).
quickstart.noRedirectText: This app has no redirect URI to return to after login.

presentation.logoUriHelp: Optional. Shown on the hosted sign-in page. An https:// address of up to 2048 characters, without a user name, password or #fragment.
presentation.clientUriHelp: Optional. The hosted sign-in page shows its host. An https:// address of up to 2048 characters, without a user name, password or #fragment.

validation.malformed: Enter a full address, such as https://app.example.com.
validation.notHttps: Use an https:// address: http and other schemes aren't accepted.
validation.credentials: Leave out the user name and password.
